Progression_Rules.name: Double Progression - Hypertrophy
Progression_Rules.trigger: All prescribed sets reach top of rep range at target RIR for 2 exposures
Progression_Rules.action: Increase load by smallest practical increment and return toward lower-middle rep range
Progression_Rules.regression: If reps repeatedly fall below minimum, hold or reduce load slightly

Progression_Rules.name: Beginner Linear Progression
Progression_Rules.trigger: All work sets completed with stable technique and target RIR
Progression_Rules.action: Add a small load next exposure
Progression_Rules.regression: Repeat; after repeated misses reduce load and rebuild
Progression_Rules.notes: Use only while progress remains repeatable.

Progression_Rules.name: Top-Set + Back-Off Strength
Progression_Rules.trigger: Top set lands inside target RIR/RPE
Progression_Rules.action: Adjust next exposure from performance trend; back-offs stay submaximal
Progression_Rules.regression: Lower target when readiness/performance trend deteriorates

Progression_Rules.name: Bodyweight Rep/Leverage Progression
Progression_Rules.applies_to: Push-ups, rows, dips, pull-ups, single-leg bodyweight work
Progression_Rules.trigger: Top rep target achieved with clean technique
Progression_Rules.action: Harder leverage, less assistance or small external load
Progression_Rules.regression: Use easier leverage or more assistance

Progression_Rules.name: Calisthenics Skill Hold Progression
Progression_Rules.trigger: Target total hold time achieved with stable body position
Progression_Rules.action: Increase hold duration or move one progression step
Progression_Rules.regression: Return to prior progression and rebuild clean volume
Progression_Rules.notes: Joint tolerance and skill quality come first.

Progression_Rules.name: Power Quality Progression
Progression_Rules.trigger: All reps remain fast/crisp with stable landing/catch
Progression_Rules.action: Small load/complexity increase or preserve load and improve output
Progression_Rules.regression: End set when speed/quality drops; reduce volume

Progression_Rules.name: Volume Progression
Progression_Rules.trigger: Performance/recovery stable >=2 weeks and target muscle needs more work
Progression_Rules.action: Add 1-2 weekly sets to target muscle
Progression_Rules.regression: Remove sets if soreness, readiness or performance worsens
Progression_Rules.notes: Do not automatically increase weekly volume.

Progression_Rules.name: Deload / Fatigue Reduction
Progression_Rules.trigger: Repeated performance decline plus elevated fatigue, or planned block end
Progression_Rules.action: Reduce sets and/or load for a short recovery week
Progression_Rules.notes: Use responsively, not as a rigid calendar rule.

Progression_Rules.name: Density / Work-Capacity Progression
Progression_Rules.action: Add small work amount or slightly reduce rest
Progression_Rules.notes: Not for heavy compounds or high-skill power work.

Progression_Rules.name: Exercise Substitution Rule
Progression_Rules.trigger: Equipment unavailable, poor fit, repeated discomfort or user preference
Progression_Rules.action: Swap within same movement pattern and training intent
Progression_Rules.notes: Preserve program intent rather than exercise identity.

Use only when recovery and adherence support high frequency.
Repeated full-body skill practice without excessive complexity.
Upper/lower permits more upper-skill exposures while preserving lower-body work.
Frequent low-fatigue skill practice fits advanced users.
Total-body sessions combine power practice and strength.
Separates high-quality power/speed and strength exposures.
Organize hard conditioning deliberately around strength work.
Dumbbell-only full body when equipment is limited.
Dumbbell upper/lower supports more weekly volume.
Stable machine patterns reduce skill demands and simplify loading.
Only when training history and recovery support specialization volume.

Research_Sources.evidence_summary: ACSM's 2026 update synthesizes 137 systematic reviews (>30,000 participants). It emphasizes consistency and individualization, training all major muscle groups at least twice weekly, heavier loads for strength, higher weekly volume for hypertrophy, and moderate loads moved fast for power.
2024 systematic review/meta-analysis reports split and full-body routines produce similar strength and hypertrophy outcomes when training volume is equated.
Meta-analysis suggests training frequency has limited independent effect on hypertrophy when weekly volume is equated; frequency remains useful for distributing weekly work.

Systematic review/meta-analysis found periodized training favored 1RM strength over non-periodized training when volume was equated; hypertrophy differences were not clear. Undulating periodization may benefit trained lifters pursuing strength.
2024 meta-regression suggests hypertrophy tends to improve as sets terminate closer to failure, while strength is less clearly dependent on RIR; the exact relationship remains uncertain.

Meta-analysis found concurrent aerobic and strength training generally does not compromise hypertrophy or maximal strength, though explosive strength can be more sensitive, especially when modalities occur in the same session.
Meta-analytic evidence supports heavier loads for maximizing dynamic strength, while hypertrophy can occur across a broad loading spectrum when effort and training volume are sufficient.
Systematic review suggests systematic exercise variation may help regional hypertrophy/strength, while excessive random variation can be counterproductive.
